guide.summary: A tiny parasite that rides on a Sunbead and slowly drains it.
guide.biology: Hitcher is made up, inspired by real parasites that live on one kind of host and take their food from it.
guide.rules: Lives in water. While free it cannot feed: it swims 0.4 cells per second, senses a Sunbead up to 3 cells away and pays 0.15 energy per second. On contact it attaches to a Sunbead that has no other Hitcher and drains 0.02 carbon per second from it, never more than the host has. Half of the drained carbon becomes Hitcher body, 0.30 becomes carbon dioxide and 0.20 metabolite, and it gains 30 energy per carbon. A Sunbead that shrinks below a quarter of its starting body dies. Hitcher rides along with its host for free and is released alive if the host dies; its own offspring are released free to find a new host. Lives up to 300 seconds.
guide.example: Add a few Hitchers to a dish of Sunbeads and watch whether the Sunbeads grow faster than the Hitchers can drain them.
